fields.index_subject_description: 55-year-old female patient with acute limb weakness
fields.chief_complaint: Progressive weakness in both legs, worsening and spreading to upper limbs/lower back

evidence.quote: A 55-year-old female patient with a history of bile duct stones treated via endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography, no prior head and neck irradiation, and a prior episode of mild hypokalemia managed with oral potassium supplementation presented with acute lower limb weakness. One day prior to admission, she noticed progressive weakness in both legs. She self-medicated with an unknown drug, and by the morning of admission, the weakness had acutely worsened and spread to the upper limbs and lower back, prompting her admission to the ICU
Once stabilized, she was transferred to the nephrology ward for further evaluation.

fields.subject: index_patient
fields.name: distal renal tubular acidosis (type 1 RTA)
fields.diagnostic_basis: Severe hypokalemia, normal anion gap metabolic acidosis, inappropriately alkaline urine and urinary electrolyte/anion-gap evaluation

evidence.quote: These findings led to a diagnosis of distal RTA (type 1 RTA)

Initial laboratory findings showed a serum potassium level as low as 1.66 mmol/L. Arterial blood gas analysis revealed normal anion gap metabolic acidosis (bicarbonate (HCO₃⁻) 15.4 mmol/L, pH 7.235, pCO₂ 37.3 mmHg), serum sodium 149.1 mmol/L, and serum chloride 118 mmol/L. Urinalysis showed alkaline urine (pH 8.0) with low specific gravity (1.006). Urinary electrolytes revealed sodium levels of 73.7 mmol/L, potassium of 11.96 mmol/L, and chloride of 76 mmol/L (Table 1). Based on the laboratory findings, the urinary potassium-to-creatinine ratio = 15.53 mmol/mmol, the serum anion gap = 15.7, and the urine anion gap = 9.66 can be readily calculated. These findings led to a diagnosis of distal RTA (type 1 RTA)
Ultrasound examination of the patient’s parotid glands revealed no abnormalities (Figure 1)

summary.text: A 55-year-old woman with prior bile-duct stones treated by ERCP and prior mild hypokalemia developed progressive weakness in both legs one day before admission. She self-treated with an unknown drug, then worsened with upper-limb and lower-back involvement. ICU potassium 1.66 mmol/L led to IV replacement and stabilization before nephrology transfer.

At nephrology examination she was alert and oriented with strength 5/5, no edema, paresthesia, nausea, headache or focal neurologic signs, pulse 78 bpm and BP 130/80 mmHg. Height was 155 cm, weight 58 kg and BMI 24.2 kg/m²; her diet was normal without restrictions. Further history found wind-triggered dry eyes and difficulty swallowing dry foods, with an enlarged non-tender right parotid.

Normal-anion-gap metabolic acidosis with bicarbonate 15.4 mmol/L, pH 7.235 and pCO2 37.3 mmHg, plus alkaline urine pH 8.0 and low specific gravity, led to type 1 distal RTA diagnosis. Author-calculated urinary K/Cr 15.53 mmol/mmol, serum anion gap 15.7 and urine anion gap 9.66 are retained with the full serum/urine table. Parotid ultrasound had no abnormalities. DEXA showed osteopenia and lumbar T-score -1.8; all regional BMD, BMC, area, T/Z scores and percentages are retained. Prose femoral-neck T-score -1.1 versus table left-neck -0.5 is quarantined.

SSA, Ro52, SSB, RNP and direct/indirect Coombs results were positive. Other named immunologic results, including negative ANA, dsDNA, Sm, Scl70, Jo1, HIV and HCV and numerical C3/C4/RF, are retained. With sicca symptoms and parotid enlargement, primary Sjögren was presumed: full criteria were not met and salivary flow, Schirmer and biopsy could not be performed. HIV was excluded; sarcoidosis was less likely, without definitive exclusion.

The patient did not desire further sicca intervention and had no other systemic manifestations aside from renal tubular abnormalities. Oral potassium chloride, sodium bicarbonate 1 mmol/kg/day and oral calcium carbonate were delivered. Ten days later her clinical condition was stable and potassium normalized at 3.95 mmol/L. No later course or immunosuppressive therapy is reported.
